title: Select, remove and Escape
prompt:
Clicking a movie's title selects it. Two things are missing:

1. **Remove** doesn't remove anything. `App`'s `handleRemove(id)` expects a movie id; fix how `MovieItem` calls `onRemove`.
2. Pressing **Escape** while focus is anywhere inside `<main>` should clear the selection, so `#selected` reads **Selected: none**.

When the selected movie is removed, the selection should also show **none**. (Look at how `selected` is calculated before adding any code for this.)
hints: Right now `onClick={onRemove}` means React calls `onRemove(event)`. Wrap it in an arrow function to pass `movie.id`.
Keyboard events bubble. One `onKeyDown` handler on `<main>` sees Escape pressed on any button inside it.
In the handler, check `e.key === 'Escape'` and call `setSelectedId(null)`.
explanation: `onClick={onRemove}` hands React a function that it calls with the click event, so `handleRemove` received an event instead of an id and filtered nothing out. `() => onRemove(movie.id)` passes exactly the argument the parent expects. Escape works from one handler on `<main>` because keydown events bubble up from the focused button. Removing the selected movie needs no extra code: `selected` is derived with `find`, so once the movie is gone it's `undefined` and the text falls back to "none".

checks.remove: Remove deletes Arrival and keeps the selection
checks.remove-selected: Removing the selected movie resets the selection to none
